{\large Ajax Benander}\\[0.3em]
{\small A field guide, not a formal paper. Lifted from the section `The Core, Stated' of \emph{Aethic Reasoning in Brief}, November 2026.\\
Every statement is abridged from the paper tagged beside it, which carries its proof and its full hypotheses; the tags are expanded in the key at the end.\\
D is a definition, P a proposition, T a theorem.}
\end{center}
\vspace{0.3em}

\noindent One object, an information state that can leave an attribute open. One algebra on it, in which a contradiction is an element and not zero. Eight posits. From these, each with a proof in the paper tagged beside it: conditioning by Bayes' rule (P\ref{prop:core_implication}); Dempster's rule of combination and the transferable belief model, with ignorance kept apart from indifference (T\ref{thm:core_evidence}); Reichenbach's screening condition and Pearl's truncated factorization (T\ref{thm:core_causal}); a classification of Newcomb-type decisions (T\ref{thm:core_decision}); the quantum--classical boundary as the partition of alternatives by their records (T\ref{thm:powerset-short}); and, with one quantitative kernel on a finite domain, the Hilbert-space representation with the Born weights and the L\"uders rule (T\ref{thm:core_kernel}). Two results part from the standard accounts: the framework's counterfactual consequence relation is extended by no preferential relation, hence by none that a similarity ordering over worlds induces (T\ref{thm:core_cf}), and its open entries cannot be read as noncontextual ignorance where the Bell inequalities are violated (T\ref{thm:core_deflation}). Seven disputes over which rule is correct, among them the Bayesian against Shafer on ignorance, the causal against the evidential theory of decision, and where the quantum--classical boundary lies, turn into questions about which structure is present (Table~\ref{tab:core_disputes}).

Table~\ref{tab:core_theories} sets each established theory or result beside what it is here, Table~\ref{tab:core_disputes} sets each dispute beside what decides it, Section~\ref{sec:core_instances} works eight instances by hand, and Table~\ref{tab:results} gives the status of every result. The arguments and the cases are in \src{Brief} and in the owner papers; the notation is that of \src{Long}.

\section{The Object}\label{sec:core_object}

\begin{definition}[Pins, attributes, states]\label{def:core_pins}
A \emph{pin} is a primitive atom. Pins carry one primitive relation, \emph{disjointness}, symmetric and irreflexive: of any two pins it is given whether they can be present together. An \emph{attribute} is a set of at least two pairwise disjoint pins. For an attribute $X$ and a set $S$ of its pins, the \emph{state} $[X : S]$ asserts that $X$ is filled by exactly the pins of $S$. It is \emph{determinate} when $S$ is a single pin and \emph{blank} when $S$ holds two or more; the state on every pin of $X$, where nothing constrains the attribute's breadth, asserts nothing; and the empty filling $[X : \varnothing]$ is \emph{invalid}. The \emph{constraint layer} is a family of finite sets of pins and states, each declared jointly invalid. Its two-pin sets are the disjointness declarations, and its other sets carry what the pins mean in use.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Representation, closure, \Aethus{}]\label{def:core_aethus}
A \emph{representation} is a set of states, read conjunctively. Its \emph{closure} $\mathrm{Cl}(R)$ is the least set of states and \emph{exclusions} $X \not\ni p$ that contains $R$ and is closed under seven rules. \emph{Narrowing}: two states on one attribute yield the state on the intersection of their fillings. \emph{Propagation}: when $R$ holds every member of a declared set but one pin $p$, of an attribute $X$, the exclusion $X \not\ni p$ is licensed, and every state $[X : F]$ narrows to $[X : F \setminus \{p\}]$. \emph{Elimination}: when every pin of $X$ but $p$ is excluded, $[X : \{p\}]$ is licensed. \emph{Invalidation}: when $R$ holds every member of a declared set that contains a state, the empty filling is licensed. \emph{Splitting}: when $R$ holds a carving (D\ref{def:core_carving}), whatever is derivable from $R$ with each of the carving's settings is licensed. \emph{Composition}: states on the components of a composite attribute and states on the composite license one another, by product and by projection. \emph{Linkage}: holding a pin that stands for an \Aethus{} licenses that \Aethus{}'s content, and holding the content licenses the pin. The empty filling is a tag and is a premise of no rule. $R$ is \emph{invalid} when $\mathrm{Cl}(R)$ contains an empty filling. Two representations are \emph{equivalent} when their closures coincide; an \emph{\Aethus{}} $A = [R]$ is an equivalence class of representations, and $\mathrm{C}(A)$ is the closure they share. The \emph{filling} $F_A(X)$ of an attribute $X$ in $A$ is the intersection of the fillings of the states of $\mathrm{C}(A)$ on $X$ with the pins of $X$ it does not exclude, and is every pin of $X$ where $\mathrm{C}(A)$ states and excludes nothing of $X$. $X$ is \emph{determinate} in $A$ when $F_A(X)$ is a single pin and \emph{blank} when it holds two or more; it is \emph{nonpresent} to $A$, blank in the retrieval sense, when $A$ leaves its entire set of pins open, $F_A(X)$ being every pin of $X$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Closure and equivalence; \src{Long}]\label{prop:core_closure}
$\mathrm{Cl}$ is extensive, monotone and idempotent, and no rule enlarges a filling. Representations that derive each other are one \Aethus{}: if $R \subseteq \mathrm{Cl}(R')$ and $R' \subseteq \mathrm{Cl}(R)$, then $[R] = [R']$. The joint pins of attributes $X_1, \ldots, X_n$, one pin from each, are pairwise disjoint and form their \emph{composite} $X_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge X_n$, and an \Aethus{} determinate on $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ is the \Aethus{} of one pin of the composite.
\end{proposition}

\section{The Two Operations}\label{sec:core_operations}

\begin{definition}[Refinement, joint assertion, addition]\label{def:core_ops}
$A$ \emph{refines} $B$, and $B$ is an \emph{ancestor} of $A$, when $\mathrm{C}(B) \subseteq \mathrm{C}(A)$. The \emph{joint assertion} $A \cdot B$ is the \Aethus{} of the union of a representation of $A$ and a representation of $B$. $B$ is a \emph{child} of $A$, and $A$ a \emph{parent} of $B$, when $B = A \cdot C$ for some $C$. The \emph{Aethic addition} $A + B$ is the sum that keeps $A$ and $B$ as its terms. Its \emph{core} is the \emph{Aethic union} $A \cup B$, the \Aethus{} whose content is $\mathrm{C}(A) \cap \mathrm{C}(B)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Meet and join; \src{Long, Tree}]\label{prop:core_ops}
$A \cdot B$ is the greatest common descendant of $A$ and $B$, and $A \cup B$ is their last common ancestor. Joint assertion is commutative, associative and idempotent, its unit is the \Aethus{} that asserts nothing, and it distributes over the addition exactly. If $A$ and $B$ are determinate on $X$ at distinct pins $a$ and $b$, the state $[X : \{a, b\}]$ lies in $\mathrm{C}(A \cup B)$ only if it lies in both $\mathrm{C}(A)$ and $\mathrm{C}(B)$: a union cannot create an agreeing state.
\end{proposition}

\section{Superposition, Carving, and the Powerset}\label{sec:core_superposition}

\begin{definition}[Agreeing superposition, broad and irreducible]\label{def:core_agreeing}
A state $[X : S]$ over two or more pins is an \emph{agreeing superposition} of $X$ over $S$ in the \emph{broad} sense: it states no exclusion among the pins of $S$, and its children $A \cdot [X : \{a\}]$, $a \in S$, may be valid. It is \emph{irreducible} in an \Aethus{} that also holds the pin $e_S$, which states that $X$ is filled by exactly $S$ and admits no narrower filling, the constraint layer declaring $e_S$ jointly invalid with every state $[X : T]$, $\varnothing \neq T \subsetneq S$. Write $I_S = [X : S] \cdot e_S$ for the irreducible agreeing superposition over $S$, and $I_{\{a\}} = [X : \{a\}]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Carving]\label{def:core_carving}
A \emph{carving} $c$ of $X$ is a partition of its pins into blocks $B_1, \ldots, B_k$. Its \emph{settings} are the states $c_j = [X : B_j]$. An \Aethus{} that holds $c$ derives whatever each of its refinements by a setting derives, and under $c$ the irreducible agreeing superposition over a filling that meets two blocks is invalid. The \emph{single-pin carving} $c_X$ has the pins of $X$ as its blocks, and every determinate state of $X$ entails it.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Carved Aethae; \src{Long}]\label{prop:core_carving}
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For a representation $R$ and a carving $c$, $[R \cup \{c\}]$ is the core of $\sum_j [R \cup \{c, c_j\}]$: an \Aethus{} that holds a carving asserts exactly what its carved refinements share.
\item[(ii)] $A \cdot [\{c\}]$ is the core of $\sum_j A \cdot [\{c, c_j\}]$: joint assertion distributes over the union of a carving's settings. It does not distribute over cores at an irreducible agreeing superposition.
\item[(iii)] If every state of a representation is determinate, every carving it holds is into single pins, and every pin it holds that stands for an \Aethus{} stands for a determinate one, then no superposition over the Aethae it yields is agreeing: any is a sum of Aethae, a disagreeing superposition of the weighted layer.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\noindent A state is identified with the sum of the irreducible agreeing superpositions over the nonempty subsets of its filling,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:core_powerset}
[X : S] \;\equiv_{\mathbf{V}}\; \sum_{\varnothing \neq Q \subseteq S} I_Q ,
\end{equation}
one term for every way the filling could stand, the terms pairwise jointly invalid; the sign is that of D\ref{def:core_tiers}. The decomposition was first made public as the General Aethic Union, in the version of \src{Long} deposited on July 1, 2025. Joint assertion with a carving strikes the terms that meet two blocks,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:core_carved}
[X : S] \cdot c \;\equiv_{\mathbf{V}}\; \sum_{j = 1}^{k} \; \sum_{\varnothing \neq Q \subseteq S \cap B_j} I_Q ,
\end{equation}
so that carving is a multiplication like any other. Writing $R \cdot [X : S] \boxplus R \cdot [X : S'] := R \cdot [X : S \cup S']$ for the \emph{agreeing sum}, a carving $c$ with $S$ inside one block and $S'$ inside another gives $c \cdot \bigl(R \cdot [X : S] \boxplus R \cdot [X : S']\bigr) \equiv_{\mathbf{V}} R \cdot [X : S] + R \cdot [X : S']$, at unit coefficients: the exclusive sum is the agreeing sum with the exclusion multiplied in \src{Long}.

\section{Weights, and the Three Tiers of Identity}\label{sec:core_weights}

\begin{definition}[Weighted Aethae]\label{def:core_weighted}
A \emph{weighted \Aethus{}} is a finite formal sum $x = \sum_i w_i A_i$ of Aethae with weights in a measure type, at the base case the non-negative reals, in which terms on one \Aethus{} combine and a term of weight zero is deleted. Joint assertion extends to weighted Aethae bilinearly. The weighted Aethae all of whose terms are invalid form the \emph{invalidity ideal}.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[The semiring; \src{Tree, Long}]\label{prop:core_semiring}
The weighted Aethae are a commutative semiring, the monoid semiring of the Aethae under joint assertion, and it is zerosumfree and additively cancellative when the measure type is. Factoring a sum through a common ancestor of its terms is an identity of the bilinear multiplication: if $A = C \cdot C_A$ and $B = C \cdot C_B$, then $aA + bB = C \cdot (a\,C_A + b\,C_B)$. An invalid \Aethus{} is an element of the semiring and is not its zero. Its joint assertion with any \Aethus{} is invalid, so the invalidity ideal is an ideal, and the quotient by it is the semiring of \emph{realizable} Aethae.
\end{proposition}

\begin{definition}[Three tiers of identity]\label{def:core_tiers}
Weighted Aethae $x$ and $y$ are \emph{equal} when they have the same terms at the same weights, invalid terms included. They are \emph{validity equivalent}, $x \equiv_{\mathbf{V}} y$, when $x + i = y + j$ for some $i$ and $j$ of the invalidity ideal, so that they are one realizable \Aethus{}; the identification~\eqref{eq:core_powerset} is made at this tier. They are \emph{projectively validity equivalent}, $x \equiv_{\mathbf{P}} y$, when $\lambda x \equiv_{\mathbf{V}} \lambda' y$ for nonzero scalars $\lambda$ and $\lambda'$, neither a zero divisor. Joint assertion passes to both quotients, and addition passes to the second and not to the third.
\end{definition}

\noindent The third tier is the Relational Weight Principle said of one \Aethus{}: no \Aethus{} carries an absolute scale, the defined quantities are ratios of weights, and the tier keeps every ratio and gives up the one common factor \src{Long}. Probabilities are valued at the second tier and are constant on the classes of the third.

\begin{definition}[Unit \Aethus{}; superposition in the weighted layer]\label{def:core_unit}
A weighted \Aethus{} $A$ is a \emph{unit \Aethus{}} when $A^{2} \equiv_{\mathbf{V}} A$; at real weights it is validity equivalent to a sum with unit coefficients over a family of valid, pairwise jointly invalid Aethae. A \emph{disagreeing superposition} of $X$ over a set $S$ of its pins is a weighted sum $\sum_{a \in S} w_a B_a$ with every $w_a$ nonzero, where $B$ is an \Aethus{} with no state on $X$ and $B_a$ is $B$ with $[X : \{a\}]$ added. For a weighted \Aethus{} $A = \sum_i w_i B_i$ the \emph{weight of a pin} $a$ of $X$ is $W_A(a) = \sum_{i \,:\, a \in F_{B_i}(X)} w_i$. $X$ is in \emph{Aethic superposition} in $A$ when two or more of its pins have nonzero weight, the general category of which the agreeing and the disagreeing superposition are the two pure forms. \emph{Might}~$a$ holds in $A$ when $W_A(a) \neq 0$, and \emph{would}~$a$ when $W_A(a)$ is the whole weight of $A$, both read relative to the weight of $A$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Implication, truth, conditional probability]\label{def:core_implication}
Let $A$ be a weighted \Aethus{} and $B$ a unit \Aethus{}. $A$ \emph{implies} $B$, $A \Rightarrow B$, when $AB \equiv_{\mathbf{V}} A$; $A \Rightarrow \lnot B$ when $AB$ is invalid; and $A$ is \emph{true relative to} $B$ when $AB$ is valid. A weighted $B$ is read through the unit \Aethus{} on its terms. For $A \equiv_{\mathbf{V}} \sum_i w_i P_i$ over valid, pairwise jointly invalid \emph{pockets} $P_i$, and statements $X$ and $Y$ of values of attributes, the \emph{conditional probability} of $Y$ given $X$ is
\[
\mathrm{P}_A(Y \,\Vert\, X) \;=\; \frac{\sum_{i \,:\, P_i \models X \wedge Y} w_i}{\sum_{i \,:\, P_i \models X} w_i} ,
\]
defined where the denominator is not zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Implication, explosion, conditioning, ontology; \src{Long}]\label{prop:core_implication}
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] If $B$ is a parent of $A$, then $A \Rightarrow B$.
\item[(ii)] As a weighted \Aethus{} an invalid \Aethus{} implies, by parenthood, what its own content holds. On the realizable Aethae its class is zero, zero times anything is zero, and it implies every \Aethus{}. Explosion is thus a statement about implication on the quotient; an invalid \Aethus{} is true relative to nothing.
\item[(iii)] Let $\{A_i\}$ be a finite family of valid, pairwise jointly invalid Aethae with real weights $w_i$ of positive total, and let $E$ be a state for which each $A_i \cdot E$ is valid or invalid outright, with indicator $v_i \in \{0, 1\}$ and $\sum_j w_j v_j > 0$. Joint assertion with $E$, read at the third tier, is the assignment $w_i \mapsto w_i v_i / \sum_j w_j v_j$: the invalid terms are dropped at the second tier and the scale at the third. The assignment satisfies the finite Kolmogorov axioms, is the conditional measure, and composes under iteration as Bayes conditionalization.
\item[(iv)] A property of weighted Aethae is \emph{ontological} when validity equivalent weighted Aethae share it. What a weighted \Aethus{} establishes and every probability read off its valid terms are ontological; the identities of its invalid terms are not.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\section{The Posits}\label{sec:core_posits}

Eight things are posited. The first four are in the wording that \src{Long} fixes, and \src{Brief} argues them.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textbf{1.}] \emph{The index (first postulate).} Any attribution of reality is a statement of relation to a particular \Aethus{}. What is indexed is content, every determinate value of a contingent attribute. The structure over Aethae, which of them are valid, what weights attach, the rule from a configuration to its record partition, is not indexed.
\item[\textbf{2.}] \emph{The constructive blank (second postulate).} If an \Aethus{} is valid, an attribute is in Aethic superposition relative to it if and only if it is nonpresent to it. A blank is an entry of the state and not ignorance of a value, and it is tense-free.
\item[\textbf{3.}] \emph{The union principle.} Jointness is primitive and exclusion is an achievement. A classical \emph{or} is a jointness whose alternatives carry declared mutual exclusions, a superposition is a jointness whose alternatives do not, and the difference is written in the alternatives and not in the logic that composes them.
\item[\textbf{4.}] \emph{Validity (third postulate).} If an \Aethus{} is valid, there is a proper child of it every proper child of which is valid: $\mathbf{V}[A] \Longrightarrow \exists B \le A\ \forall C \le B\ \mathbf{V}[C]$. The quantifier form is selected by elimination within a class of rules that are based on refinement and independent of weight \src{Brief, Long}; that the rule lies in that class is what is posited.
\item[\textbf{5.}] \emph{Composition.} Joint assertion is the multiplication of Aethae and the Aethic addition their sum (D\ref{def:core_ops}).
\item[\textbf{6.}] \emph{The semiring.} Weights are non-negative, and an invalid \Aethus{} is an element that stands with its weight and is zero only in the quotient (P\ref{prop:core_semiring}). This is a choice of design.
\item[\textbf{7.}] \emph{The kernel.} The quantum weights are those of a compositional path kernel (T\ref{thm:core_kernel}). It is the one quantitative posit.
\item[\textbf{8.}] \emph{The bridge.} A formally invalid \Aethus{} is physically unrealizable. It is a principle and not a theorem, and it is the one place at which the formal apparatus meets what is observed.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{definition}[Proper child, reduced form]\label{def:core_proper}
$B$ is a \emph{proper child} of $A$, $B \le A$, when $A$ admits an admissible declared decomposition $A \rightsquigarrow bB + cC$ in which $b$ is nonzero and not negligible relative to $c$, which at real weights is $b > 0$; a \emph{proper descendant} is a proper child at any depth. Every \Aethus{} is a proper child of itself. A weighted \Aethus{} $x$ is a \emph{proper parent} of $y$ when $x = y + z$ for some weighted \Aethus{} $z$, and is \emph{proper} when no invalid \Aethus{} is a proper child of it. The \emph{reduced form} $\bar{x}$ is the greatest nonzero proper weighted \Aethus{} of which $x$ is a proper parent, where there is one.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[The fixed point; \src{Tree, Long}]\label{prop:core_fixed}
Let $\mathrm{Base}$ be the Aethae invalid without recursion, by a direct contradiction or by the contrapositive of the second postulate, and let proper childhood be reflexive and transitive, as it is under the composition property of the measure type. Put $F(Y) = \{A \notin \mathrm{Base} : \exists B \le A\ \forall C \le B,\ C \in Y\}$ and $G(Z) = \mathrm{Base} \cup \{A : \forall B \le A\ \exists C \le B,\ C \in Z\}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $F$ and $G$ are monotone, and the greatest fixed point of $F$ and the least fixed point of $G$, the \emph{doomed} Aethae, are complements.
\item[(ii)] The third postulate says that validity is a post-fixed point of $F$. Where invalidity is generated by the base cases, validity is the greatest fixed point of $F$.
\item[(iii)] Both fixed points are reached at the first stage: an \Aethus{} is doomed exactly when every proper descendant of it has a base case beneath it.
\item[(iv)] In a model with finitely many attributes the doomed Aethae are the ones closure tags invalid, and they form a multiplicative ideal, so that validity is an exact quotient of the algebra.
\item[(v)] At real weights a weighted \Aethus{} has a nonzero reduced form exactly when one of its terms is not doomed, and the third postulate reads: a weighted \Aethus{} without a reduced form is invalid.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Conditional record exclusion; \src{Realist, Quant}]\label{prop:core_record_exclusion}
Let $A_{\mathrm{coh}}$ assert a maintained coherence, and let the base contradictions be the joint statings of that coherence with a record that separates its alternatives. If every proper descendant of $A_{\mathrm{coh}}$ has a further proper descendant that states such a record, then $A_{\mathrm{coh}}$ is invalid, invalidity being generated by the base cases.
\end{proposition}

\noindent Two consequences of the posits are used throughout. \emph{Extrusion}: a superposition and its resolution are not the earlier and the later state of one history. Relative to the prior \Aethus{} the superposition stands, relative to the posterior one it never stood, and collapse is a change of index and not an event \src{Long}. \emph{The fundamental theorem of Aethic reasoning}: to every valid uncertainty principle there corresponds a coherence principle, so that what is permanently blank stands in agreeing superposition; and wherever the third postulate can land a contradiction of an attribute's agreeing claim, the attribute is carved along the classes the records separate \src{Long}.

\section{The Theorems}\label{sec:core_theorems}

\begin{theorem}[The counterfactual consequence relation; \src{Modal}]\label{thm:core_cf}
For an \Aethus{} $A$, an antecedent $X$ on the attributes $Q_X$ and a scope $\sigma$, let the \emph{reopening} $A \ominus_\sigma Q_X$ be the priority-selected maximal closed restrictions of $A$ that keep the content the scope protects and are blank on the attributes it clears; let the \emph{perturbation} $\pi^{\sigma}_X(A)$ be the union, over these, of the maximal consistent refinements that satisfy $X$, its \emph{pockets}; and let $X \mid\sim_A Y$ hold when every visible pocket affirms $Y$, the \emph{might} holding when some does and the grade being the weighted proportion. In finite models with positive weight on every pocket, a conjunctive antecedent reopening each of its constituent attributes:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $\mid\sim_A$ satisfies Reflexivity, Right Weakening, And, Or, Left Logical Equivalence at attribute grade, and Cut where the reopenings are nested;
\item[(ii)] an entry of $A$ outside the cleared scope, and joined to it by no support chain, recorded wiring or joint constraint, is stated in every pocket;
\item[(iii)] there is a state on four attributes at which Cautious Monotony fails, and Rational Monotony with it, so that no preferential consequence relation extends $\mid\sim_A$, and none induced by a similarity ordering over worlds.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Openness is not noncontextual ignorance; \src{Realist, Quant, Long}]\label{thm:core_deflation}
Call an assignment a \emph{lossless deflation} of $A$ when it gives, for $A$ and every state $B$ of its refinement structure, a family $W(B)$ of complete valuations such that each valuation assigns every attribute one value, independently of which other attributes are stated or measured, and agrees with the stated entries of $B$; on the exclusive fragment $B$ is valid exactly when $W(B)$ is nonempty, refinement restricting the family; and the statistics over any attributes of $A$ are the marginals of one probability measure on $W(A)$, the choice of measured attributes being independent of the valuation. If the blank attributes of $A$ contain four whose CHSH combination exceeds $2$, no lossless deflation of $A$ exists.
\end{theorem}

\noindent \emph{The record partition} \src{Quant, Long}. For $n$ slits and a configuration of detectors, the \emph{signature} of a slit is the tuple of the detectors that fire on its traversal, and the slits of equal signature form the classes $E_1, \ldots, E_k$. 

\begin{theorem}[Powerset Invalidation; \src{Quant, Long}]\label{thm:powerset-short} Assume the declared record structure is complete and persistent: the signatures include all relevant accessible records, and every proper descendant retains a descendant stating a separating record whenever the candidate spans signature classes. Then every subset $T$ of the $n$ slits---every candidate claim ``the particle traverses exactly these slits in coherent superposition''---falls, relative to an \Aethus{} in which the detector configuration is stated and over the specified candidate domain, into exactly one of three bins: (i) \emph{valid}: $T$ is empty or equals one full equivalence class; (ii) \emph{over-specified}, invalid by record-individuation: $T$ is a nonempty proper subset of a single class, drawing a distinction that no information could ever support; (iii) \emph{third-postulate invalid}: $T$ spans two or more classes, combining alternatives some record can distinguish, so that a future refinement can expose the maintained coherence as contradictory---checkmate, in the sense of P\ref{prop:core_fixed}. The bins are mutually exclusive and jointly exhaustive, with the counts explicit: $k$ valid nonempty cases, $\sum_j (2^{|E_j|} - 2)$ over-specified cases, and the remainder third-postulate.
\end{theorem}

\noindent Alternatives of equal signature are not distinct alternatives of any attribute. Under classical randomization over configurations whose markers are orthogonal, the attainable pairs of visibility and distinguishability are the triangle $V + D \le 1$, and no kernel weight is consulted in deriving it.

\begin{theorem}[The kernel, and the Hilbert representation; \src{Quant}]\label{thm:core_kernel}
Posit, for a system with a finite set $X$ of paths, each ending at a readout configuration $x(p) \in \Sigma$, a kernel $\mathcal{K}$ on paths, multiplicative under concatenation, with (K1) the weight of a cluster $T \subseteq X$ at $x$ being $W_x(T) = \bigl|\sum_{p \in T,\, x(p) = x} \mathcal{K}(p)\bigr|^{2}$ and $W(T) = \sum_x W_x(T)$; (K2) the propagator unitary; and (K3) $W_x(T)/W(T)$ the frequency of the readout $x$ on runs prepared in $T$. Put $|T\rangle = \sum_{p \in T} \mathcal{K}(p)\,|x(p)\rangle$ in $\ell^{2}(\Sigma)$. Then, on the finite readout slices:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] a valid cluster in the agreeing regime is the vector $|T\rangle$, of squared norm $W(T)$, and for disjoint clusters $|T_1 \cup T_2\rangle = |T_1\rangle + |T_2\rangle$;
\item[(ii)] for a record labeling of the readout configurations with classes $\Sigma_j$, $E_j$ the paths that end in $\Sigma_j$ and $P_j$ the projector onto the span of $\Sigma_j$, $|T \cap E_j\rangle = P_j |T\rangle$, so that record observables are self-adjoint operators, a theorem of the second and third postulates given the assignment;
\item[(iii)] the probability of the outcome $j$ on $T$ is $W(T \cap E_j)/W(T) = \lVert P_j |T\rangle \rVert^{2}/\langle T | T \rangle$;
\item[(iv)] conditioning on a stated record, a stipulated record-compatible restriction, is pruning followed by renormalization and equals $P_j \rho P_j / \mathrm{Tr}(P_j \rho)$, the L\"uders rule;
\item[(v)] the space of a composite setup is the tensor product of its factors' spaces, evolution is unitary by (K2), and for a fixed record partition $\sum_j \lVert P_j |T\rangle \rVert^{2} = \langle T | T \rangle$, so that the statistics of every observable commuting with the partition are unchanged by the record.
\end{enumerate}
The weights determine the kernel values at each configuration up to a gauge, by polarization; the reconstruction across configurations is not proved. A representation of every ray is impossible on one fixed finite domain of dimension two or more.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Screening, and intervention; \src{Causal}]\label{thm:core_causal}
Let a state in disagreeing superposition on finitely many finite attributes be presented as a product of entries, each a hard constraint and a non-negative weight on the alternatives of a set of attributes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] If the weight on $(A, B, C)$ factors as $f(a, c)\, g(b, c)$, then $W(a, b \mid c) = W(a \mid c)\, W(b \mid c)$ at every pocket of $C$ of positive weight.
\item[(ii)] If $A$ and $B$ are correlated, a chain of entries joins them, and either some entry touches both or the attributes that share an entry with $A$ separate $A$ from $B$. Every family that separates $A$ from $B$ screens them, and a family that screens them is correlated with each and carries their whole covariance: the structure of Reichenbach's principle of the common cause.
\item[(iii)] For a state given by a history of mechanisms, $W(v) = \prod_k e_k(v_k \mid \mathrm{in}_k)$, settling $V_k$ to $x$ gives $\mathbf{1}[v_k = x] \prod_{j \neq k} e_j(v_j \mid \mathrm{in}_j)$, Pearl's truncated factorization; and every causal Bayesian network is such a history.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Decision, in two regimes; \src{Decision}]\label{thm:core_decision}
For a deliberating state and a candidate act, the binding modes of the couplings being supplied, let the settled law of the payoff-relevant attributes be obtained by fixing the act, retaining the couplings that bind in deliberation, detaching the others jointly, and conditioning on the stated evidence, and let the rule be the maximization of settled expected utility over the acts whose settling leaves a residue of positive weight. If the settled law factorizes so as to be the same for every act, comparison of the acts pocket by pocket is sound and dominance applies. If the settled laws of two admissible acts differ, the acts are compared on their whole residues and dominance is not guaranteed. Newcomb's problem with a predictor whose accuracy holds whatever the act is of the second kind, and the rule one-boxes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evidence, on one attribute; \src{Evidence}]\label{thm:core_evidence}
Let $X$ have finitely many pins, every nonempty set of which is a valid filling, let a \emph{mass function} $m$ be non-negative weights of total one on the nonempty sets of pins, and put $A_m = \sum_S m(S)\,[X : S]$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] With~\eqref{eq:core_powerset}, the realizable Aethae of $X$ are the non-negative functions on the nonempty sets of pins, under pointwise sum and product, $I_Q$ being the function that is one at $Q$ and zero elsewhere. No valid \Aethus{} is identified with zero.
\item[(ii)] $A_{m_1} \cdot A_{m_2}$ is, at the three tiers of D\ref{def:core_tiers}, the conjunctive combination of $m_1$ and $m_2$ with their conflict on invalid Aethae; that combination with the conflict removed; and Dempster's rule of combination, which is Bayes' rule when every set of positive mass is a single pin.
\item[(iii)] The coefficients of $A_m$ on the $I_Q$ are $q_m(Q) = \sum_{S \supseteq Q} m(S)$, the commonality function, and joint assertion multiplies them.
\item[(iv)] The $A_m$ are, up to scale, a proper subcone of the realizable Aethae, and $I_Q$ over two or more pins lies outside it. Joint assertion with a state narrows a broad state and leaves an irreducible superposition standing or makes it invalid.
\item[(v)] On an attribute whose valid fillings are its single pins, $A_m \equiv_{\mathbf{V}} \sum_a \bigl(\sum_{S \ni a} m(S)\bigr)\,[X : \{a\}]$, and total ignorance over a set of pins is projectively validity equivalent to the uniform distribution on it.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Regime; \src{Union}]\label{thm:core_regime}
Given the primitive composition of alternatives and the exclusions their interiors state, the regime of the composition, joint, constrained or fully exclusive, is determined by the pattern of those exclusions. No second primitive of composition distinguishes the joint regime from the exclusive one, and changing only the interiors carries one composition from the first to the second.
\end{theorem}

\section{Disputes, Located}\label{sec:core_disputes}

Seven of the framework's results have one form. A dispute between rules, each defended as the correct one, becomes a question about the object: which structure it has, at which tier of identity it is read, or at which declared setting an operation is run on it. The framework states the condition, and each rule is what the object gives on one side of it. No rule is selected in general; where the condition is decided for an object, the dispute is decided for that object. Table~\ref{tab:core_disputes} lists the cases. Each row holds at the grade of the statement it cites: the decision row is on the settling rule, which is adopted and not derived, and the boundary row is relative to a declared record structure. Under the premises stated for each case, the smoking lesion falls on the first side of the decision condition and Newcomb's problem with an act-robust predictor on the second \src{Decision}.

\section{Instances, by Hand}\label{sec:core_instances}

\noindent Each is a minute's check against the statements above.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textbf{1.}] \emph{Narrowing, and contradiction} \src{Evidence}. Let $X$ have pins $a$, $b$, $c$. By~\eqref{eq:core_powerset}, $[X : \{a, b\}] \cdot [X : \{a, c\}] \equiv_{\mathbf{V}} (I_{\{a\}} + I_{\{b\}} + I_{\{a,b\}})(I_{\{a\}} + I_{\{c\}} + I_{\{a,c\}}) \equiv_{\mathbf{V}} I_{\{a\}}$: two blanks narrow to what they share. And $I_{\{a,b\}} \cdot [X : \{a, c\}]$ is invalid: a superposition over $a$ and $b$ that admits no narrower filling is contradicted by evidence that excludes $b$.
\item[\textbf{2.}] \emph{Bayes' rule} \src{Long, Evidence}. Prior weights $0.2$ and $0.8$ on $a$ and $b$, and an observation with likelihoods $0.9$ and $0.3$. The product $(0.2\,[X : \{a\}] + 0.8\,[X : \{b\}]) \cdot (0.9\,[X : \{a\}] + 0.3\,[X : \{b\}])$ has the valid terms $0.18\,[X : \{a\}] + 0.24\,[X : \{b\}]$ and the weight $0.78$ on the contradiction of $a$ with $b$. Dropping the contradiction is the second tier and rescaling the third: $\tfrac{3}{7}\,[X : \{a\}] + \tfrac{4}{7}\,[X : \{b\}]$.
\item[\textbf{3.}] \emph{Zadeh's example} \src{Evidence}. One physician gives meningitis $0.99$ and a tumor $0.01$, another concussion $0.99$ and the tumor $0.01$. Their joint assertion carries $0.9999$ on contradictions between diagnoses and $0.0001$ on the tumor. At the first tier it is that sum, the combination of the transferable belief model; at the second, $0.0001$ on the tumor; at the third, the tumor, which is the verdict of Dempster's rule. The first tier records that $0.9999$ of the weight was contradiction.
\item[\textbf{4.}] \emph{Ignorance is not indifference} \src{Evidence}. On pins $a$ and $b$, total ignorance is $[X : \{a, b\}] \equiv_{\mathbf{V}} I_{\{a\}} + I_{\{b\}} + I_{\{a,b\}}$ and the uniform distribution is $\tfrac12 I_{\{a\}} + \tfrac12 I_{\{b\}}$. They differ at $I_{\{a,b\}}$ and are different classes at the third tier. On an attribute whose valid fillings are its single pins the first is $I_{\{a\}} + I_{\{b\}}$, twice the second, and the two are one class.
\item[\textbf{5.}] \emph{Four slits, one detector} \src{Long, Quant}. Slits $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, and a detector that fires on $A$ or $B$ without recording which. The classes are $\{A, B\}$ and $\{C, D\}$. Of the sixteen sets of slits, T\ref{thm:powerset-short} leaves valid the empty set and the two classes; $\{A\}$, $\{B\}$, $\{C\}$ and $\{D\}$ are over-specified; and the nine sets that meet both classes are invalid by the third postulate. With no detector there is one class, and of the nonempty sets it alone is valid.
\item[\textbf{6.}] \emph{Complementarity from mixing} \src{Quant, Brief}. A tag marks the path, with orthogonal markers, on a fraction $p$ of the runs. On the marked runs the paths compose as exclusive alternatives, with distinguishability $D = 1$ and visibility $V = 0$; on the unmarked runs they are one agreeing pair, with $D = 0$ and $V = 1$. Weights add: $D = p$, $V = 1 - p$ and $V + D = 1$, with no kernel consulted.
\item[\textbf{7.}] \emph{A counterfactual that no ordering gives} \src{Modal}. Attributes: rain $x$, the sprinkler $s$, a wet lawn $y$, overflowing gutters $z$. Declared invalid: $s$ with $\lnot y$, and $x$ with $s$ and $\lnot z$. The sprinkler is the declared ground of the wet lawn. The state says $s$, hence $y$, and leaves the rain and the gutters open. \emph{If it had rained}: one pocket, $(x, s, y, z)$, so the lawn would be wet and the gutters would overflow. \emph{If it had rained and the lawn had been wet}, the conjunction reopening both of its attributes: reopening the lawn clears its ground, the pockets are $(x, s, y, z)$, $(x, \lnot s, y, z)$ and $(x, \lnot s, y, \lnot z)$, and the gutters might not overflow. Cautious Monotony fails.
\item[\textbf{8.}] \emph{Newcomb's threshold} \src{Decision}. The transparent box holds $t$, the opaque prize is $M$, and the predictor errs at the rate $\varepsilon$. With the accuracy coupling retained, the settled expected utilities are $(1 - \varepsilon) M$ for one box and $t + \varepsilon M$ for two, so one box wins exactly when $\varepsilon < \tfrac12 - t/2M$; for $t = 10^{3}$ and $M = 10^{6}$, when $\varepsilon < 0.4995$.
\end{enumerate}
